stops.name: The threefold healing: the prophet teaches medicine by knife, herb and word
stops.campa: The prophet gives the world the arts of healing, for to keep the good creation whole is itself a war against the Lie that brings sickness and death. He teaches three medicines: healing by the knife, the surgeon's craft; healing by the herb, the virtue of the good plants the Wise Lord made; and healing by the holy word, the recited spell of the Manthra, which of the three is the most powerful, for it reaches the soul. The physician who heals with the sacred word heals best of all. So the faith takes the body as well as the soul into its care, against the demon of disease.

stops.name: The marriage to Hvovi, the household and the children of the prophet
stops.campa: At the court the prophet takes to wife Hvovi, daughter of the noble Frashaoshtra, of the counselor-house of the kingdom. From his marriages come six children who will carry the seed of the religion: the sons Isadvastar, Urvatatnar and Khvarshedcheher, and the daughters Freni, Thriti and Pouruchista, the youngest, to whom he gives counsel in his own hymns when he weds her to the sage Jamasp. Around him now stands a household of the faith, a family of the Good Religion, and the prophet's line is set to run down the ages toward the Saviors who are to come.
stops.quote: This is well known to the wooers and to thee, O Pouruchista, youngest of the daughters of Zarathustra: he gives thee as a helpmate one who is strong in the Good Mind and in Truth.
stops.quote_source: Gathas, Yasna 53.3 (paraphrase of the Vahishtoisht Gatha)

stops.name: The seven regions, the sending-out of the faith and the feast of the new day
stops.campa: From the throne of Bactria the Good Religion goes out to the seven climes of the earth. The prophet sends teachers and priests across the Iranian lands, and the fire-altars multiply from Chorasmia to Sistan. He hallows the turning of the year: at the vernal equinox, when day conquers night, the feast of Nowruz is kept, the new day, sign and rehearsal of the last renewal of the world, when the Wise Lord will make all things wonderful. The whole ordered year becomes a liturgy of the war of light, each festival a station on the road from the first creation to the Making-Wonderful at the end.
stops.quote: May we be those who shall make this world wonderful, when it shall be renewed — we, the saviours of the world, through the will of the Wise Lord.

stops.name: The first war against Arjasp of Turan, the demand and the battle
stops.campa: Arjasp, king of Turan and champion of the demon-worship, sends to Vishtaspa demanding that he abandon the Good Religion and return to the old idols, or face war. On the prophet's counsel the king refuses. The Turanian hosts pour into Iran, and a terrible battle is joined. Vishtaspa's brother Zarir falls in the field, and the aged Lohrasp with him; but Prince Isfandiyar, brazen-bodied and unconquerable, breaks the enemy and drives Arjasp back beyond the river. The first holy war is won, and the fire-faith stands defended by the sword as well as the word.

stops.name: The Bridge of the Separator, the Chinvat and the judgment of souls
stops.campa: The prophet teaches the last things. At death every soul waits three days by the body, and on the fourth dawn comes to the Chinvat Bridge, the Bridge of the Separator, where its deeds are weighed. To the just the bridge grows broad, and a fair maiden, the soul's own good conscience, leads it to the House of Song, the paradise of light. To the wicked the bridge narrows to a razor's edge, a foul hag meets it, and it falls into the House of the Lie. Those whose good and ill are equal wait in Hamistagan between. Every choice in life is met again at the Bridge.
stops.quote: When shall I know, O Wise One, that ye have power over any whom my tongue threatens? Let the reward of the followers of Truth be told me.

stops.name: Lake Kansaoya, the seed of the prophet and the Saviour to come
stops.campa: The prophet reveals the end of the world. His own seed is kept, guarded by thousands of holy spirits, in the waters of Lake Kansaoya in the land of the lake-basin. At the last times, in three appointed ages, three Saviours will be born of it: a virgin will bathe in the miraculous water, conceive by the seed of Zarathustra, and bear the Saoshyant, the last Saviour, who will raise the dead, make the molten metal flow like warm milk over the good, put down the demon and the Lie forever, and renew the whole world in the Making-Wonderful. The prophet's line reaches to the resurrection itself.

stops.name: The second war and the sack of Balkh: Arjasp returns
stops.campa: After long peace Arjasp of Turan gathers his hosts again and, while Isfandiyar is away or in chains, falls upon Bactra by surprise. The Turanians storm the city, mother of cities, and put it to fire and sword. They break into the great temple where the sacred fire burns and slaughter the priests of the Good Religion at their altars. The aged prophet, now seventy-seven years old, is within, keeping the fire of Nush-Adar. The Lie has come at last with an army to the very sanctuary of the Truth.

stops.name: The fire-altar of Nush-Adar, the death of the prophet at seventy-seven
stops.campa: At the fire-altar in Balkh, praying before the flame, the prophet is struck down. A Turanian of the old enemy, the karapan Bradres, the very kind of sorcerer who tried to kill him at his birth, comes on him from behind and slays him at the fire he has tended all his life, in the seventy-seventh year of his age. As he falls he hurls his rosary at the murderer, who dies of it; the Truth is not defenceless even in death. So the one who laughed at his birth dies at his altar and passes over his own Bridge into the House of Song.
stops.quote: As the holy one I recognize thee, Mazda Ahura, when I saw thee in the beginning at the birth of Life.
